turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm buying a game for my parents, they're in their seventies and have never played anything modern.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me get through all the options before you weigh in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a tile laying one where you build a little medieval landscape together, very calm, about forty minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then a quick word game with letter tiles, sort of like crosswords but faster and less serious.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A trivia game with questions from every decade, which my dad would probably love and my mum might hate.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or a gentle train route game where you collect coloured cards and claim lines across a map.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Alright, I'm finished. What's your opinion?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: I'd go train routes or tiles, both are classics for new players because every turn is just one small choice. The word game is great if they like crosswords, and trivia is risky with your mum.
